vision_features.summary: A grass stem (likely a cereal crop such as wheat or rice) has been split lengthwise to reveal the internal structure, which is almost entirely replaced by dry, pale grey-white to silvery, shredded and collapsed fibrous tissue across its full length. The outer sheath remains brown and papery, fraying at the edges. Irregular dark grey to black patches are embedded within the pale interior tissue, particularly toward the central section. The stem interior is the most severely affected organ, and the most striking feature is the complete replacement of normal pith with bleached, dry, longitudinally shredded fibrous material, suggesting severe internal deterioration throughout the sampled stem length.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Cercospora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Leaves are typically only discolored on the upper surface with symptoms ranging from light purple, pinpoint spots to larger, irregularly shaped patches. Affected leaves may become leathery and dark purple with bronze highlights.. Symptoms occur only on the upper leaf surface (unlike sunburn which occurs on the leaf underside), and affected leaves appear leathery, dark purple, and/or bronze. Severe disease can cause defoliation but petioles remain attached to the plant.. Soybean rust, Soybean Vein necrosis virus, Herbicide injury, Sunscald

Knowledge-base entry for 'Charcoal_Rot':
────────────────────────────────────────
Initial symptoms are patches of stunted or wilted plants with leaves remaining attached after plant death. The lower stem and taproots develop a discolored light gray or charcoal-like appearance due to numerous tiny, black fungal structures called microsclerotia.. Numerous tiny, black microsclerotia scattered throughout the pith and on the surface of taproots and lower stems, giving a charcoal-like gray discoloration. Leaves remain attached after plant death.. Diaporthe complex (pod and stem blight and stem canker), Phytophthora root and stem rot, Soybean cyst nematode, Sudden death syndrome, White mold, Anthracnose stem blight, Brown stem rot, Late season frost damage, Drought, Lightning damage

Ruling feature : Location of symptoms: Cercospora affects only leaf upper surfaces with purple/bronze discoloration, while Charcoal Rot affects lower stems and taproots with charcoal-gray discoloration from black microsclerotia
Cercospora: Purple to bronze discoloration restricted to the upper leaf surface, making leaves appear leathery and dark; defoliation may occur but petioles remain attached.
Charcoal_Rot: Light gray to charcoal-like discoloration of the lower stem and taproots caused by numerous tiny black microsclerotia; leaves remain attached to the plant after death.
